name: Asian American Studies
summary: Asian American Studies explores the histories, cultures, and experiences of Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders in the United States. Students examine immigration, community, identity, and civil rights.
description: Asian American Studies emerged from student activism in the late 1960s and examines Asian American life from early Chinese and Japanese immigration through the Chinese Exclusion Act, Japanese American incarceration during World War II, post-1965 immigration, refugee communities from Southeast Asia, and today's diverse communities. Coursework draws on history, sociology, literature, film, and law and addresses topics such as racism, labor, gender, family, and political activism. Many programs include community-based learning. Graduates work in education, community organizations, social services, policy, law, and media.
